title: Reconstruction of operadic sections from coherent colored operations
statement:
Use quasicategories, nerves, coherent functor categories, full subcategories and mapping spaces of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], cocartesian fibrations of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], and the definitions of symmetric infinity-operads and relative algebra categories in [lem-coef-relative-operadic-terminal-active-mapping]. Fix sufficiently large universes. Let $O$ be a small ordinary symmetric colored operad: it has a set of colors, sets of operations with each finite labeled list of inputs and one output, permutation actions, unary identities, and associative unital equivariant substitution; nullary operations are allowed. Write $\langle n\rangle=\{*,1,\ldots,n\}$ and let $\mathrm{Fin}_*$ have these finite pointed sets as objects and pointed maps as arrows. Its category of operators $O^\otimes$ has finite tuples of colors as objects. An arrow over $f:\langle n\rangle\to\langle k\rangle$ is one operation $(c_i)_{f(i)=j}\to d_j$ for each $j\ne *$; discarded inputs contribute no operation. Composition is substitution. Let $q:E^\otimes\to N(O^\otimes)$ be a cocartesian fibration which is a map of infinity-operads. For a color $c$, write $E_c$ for the degreewise fibre over the one-term tuple $(c)$. Suppose inert projections identify $E^\otimes_{(c_1,\ldots,c_n)}\simeq\prod_i E_{c_i}$, including the empty product. For an operation $\theta:(c_1,\ldots,c_r)\to d$, denote its transport functor by $T_\theta:\prod_iE_{c_i}\to E_d$.

Inert-preserving sections of $q$ can be reconstructed from the following data, and restriction to these data is an equivalence of infinity-categories. Choose $x_c\in E_c$ for each color and a structure arrow $T_\theta(x_{c_1},\ldots,x_{c_r})\to x_d$ for each operation. For unary identity operations this is the identity equivalence under $T_{1_c}\simeq\mathrm{id}_{E_c}$. Require that the associated total arrows over inert operators are $q$-cocartesian, compatibly with their compositions; the structure arrows displayed above lie in the target color fibre, whereas the associated total arrows are obtained by preceding them with the chosen transport lifts. Include the identity and permutation compatibilities and all homotopy coherent substitution compatibilities: for each finite rooted tree labeled by operations, all comparison simplices between evaluating its vertices successively and evaluating any contractions of its inner edges, compatible with further contractions, grafting and insertion of unary identities. A nullary vertex uses the empty-input transport. These compatibilities are data in the mapping spaces, not merely equalities in a homotopy category. Coherences for a forest are the products of those for its output trees, pulled back along the corresponding projections of the external inputs; inputs sent to the basepoint are omitted.

The reconstructed section has value $(x_{c_1},\ldots,x_{c_n})$ under the Segal equivalence. Its arrow over $f$ has output $j$ equal to the structure arrow of the operation on $f^{-1}(j)$; its composition simplices are the specified substitution simplices. A transformation is reconstructed from maps of the color objects and the compatible operation-naturality simplices and all higher substitution compatibilities. The same reconstruction holds with arbitrary simplicial parameter $K$: color objects are functors $K\to E_c$, operation arrows are coherent transformations, and the higher compatibility data are parameterized over $K$. It commutes with restrictions in $K$, restriction to suboperads, and projection to any chosen colors. The space of reconstructions equipped with their identification with the specified data is contractible. This assertion imposes no limit, colimit, or presentability hypothesis.

source.place: Higher Algebra (2017), Construction 2.1.1.7, Definition 2.1.1.10, Example 2.1.1.21 and Definition 2.1.3.1 and Remark 2.1.3.4; coherent outputwise reconstruction formulation of the operator-category Segal axioms. Source inspected online; WANTED archive in literature/. No Stacks tag treats infinity-operadic coherent sections.

proof.text:
Put $B=N(O^\otimes)$. Use the relative-algebra definition of [lem-coef-relative-operadic-terminal-active-mapping] only, not that node's terminal-active theorem. Write $\Gamma_I(q)$ for its full category of inert-preserving sections. Choose representatives $X_{\mathbf c}$ for the inverse images of $(x_{c_1},\ldots,x_{c_n})$ under the assumed equivalence $E_{\mathbf c}\simeq\prod_iE_{c_i}$, with the identification included. These choices have contractible spaces of choices: apply a quasi-inverse of the equivalence, and its unit and counit identify each homotopy fiber with a point. For an operator $f:\mathbf c\to\mathbf d$ let $\theta_j:(c_i)_{f(i)=j}\to d_j$ be its output operations, and let $M_f(X,Y)$ be the homotopy fiber over this particular operator of $\operatorname{Map}_{E^\otimes}(X,Y)\to\operatorname{Map}_B(\mathbf c,\mathbf d)$. The base mapping space is discrete. The mapping-space Segal axiom, explicitly included in [lem-coef-relative-operadic-terminal-active-mapping], gives an output product, both in $E^\otimes$ and in $B$. Taking fibers over the tuple $(\theta_j)_j$ gives the relative output product. For its $j$th factor, first project the source inertly onto the subtuple indexed by $f^{-1}(j)$ and then use the active operator $\theta_j$. Precomposition by the inert cocartesian lift, followed by the active cocartesian lift, identifies that factor, by [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion], with the mapping space in the target color fiber. Hence there is a natural equivalence
$$M_f(X_{\mathbf c},X_{\mathbf d})\simeq\prod_{j=1}^{|\mathbf d|}\operatorname{Map}_{E_{d_j}}\bigl(T_{\theta_j}((x_{c_i})_{f(i)=j}),x_{d_j}\bigr).$$
Use the inert projections that induce the stated fiber identifications. They are inert for the total operad and lie over the canonical inert operators of $B$. They are also $q$-cocartesian: write $p_B:B\to N(\mathrm{Fin}_*)$ and $p_E=p_Bq$. The mapping square for a $p_E$-cocartesian projection is the outer rectangle formed from its $q$-mapping square and the mapping square of its $p_B$-cocartesian image. The outer rectangle and the latter square are homotopy pullbacks, hence so is the former, by substituting the two path-fiber-product formulas. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion] to $q$. In this calculation we use both the fiber and the mapping-space Segal axioms, not merely the displayed fiber equivalence in the item. If the target tuple is empty the product is a point; a zero-input factor is the nullary transport, not a missing factor.

source.place: Construction 2.1.1.7; Definition 2.1.1.10(1)-(3), especially its mapping-space condition; Remark 2.1.1.14. The relative mapping-space calculation is written out here.

proof.text: For a section $s$, its inert projections identify $s(\mathbf c)$ with $X_{\mathbf c}$, where $x_c=s(c)$. For an active one-output operator $\theta$, choose a $q$-cocartesian lift $u_\theta:X_{\mathbf c}\to T_\theta(X_{\mathbf c})$. The section edge $s(\theta)$ corresponds to a vertical arrow $a_\theta:T_\theta(X_{\mathbf c})\to x_d$ under the mapping-fiber equivalence in [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport] with parameter $\Delta^0$: it is characterized by a triangle $a_\theta u_\theta\simeq s(\theta)$ over $\theta$. Thus one factors the active edge through its active transport; one does not compose it with an inert transport to obtain $a_\theta$. That theorem applies because $q$ is an inner fibration with cocartesian lifts, and [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion] identifies its horn and mapping-square notions. Identity operators use the degenerate lift, and substitution uses the composition clause of [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-composition-initiality]. Inert operators give the corresponding cocartesian projection edges; permutations are the inert bijective case. Apply the pointwise transport theorem with each simplex or coherence-parameter shape to factor the triangles and their higher simplices together. This gives the specified coherent operation data, not just its images in homotopy categories.

source.place: Definition 2.1.3.1, together with cocartesian factorization (HTT 2.4.4.2-3, duals, carried by the cited pointwise-transport node).

proof.text: Here is the combinatorial meaning of the supplied all-higher tree data used in the converse. A simplex of $B$ is a chain $\mathbf c^0\xrightarrow{f_1}\cdots\xrightarrow{f_m}\mathbf c^m$. At level $a$ place a vertex labeled by $\theta_{a,j}$ at each output $j$ of $f_a$, and attach its input wires to the preceding level. This is a leveled forest, not in general a single rooted tree. A wire sent to the basepoint stops at that level. Keep the forests of every subinterval of levels as well: an operation performed before its output is discarded must still appear on the earlier face. For each interval $[a,b]$ and each nonempty output wire at level $b$, its ancestors give one rooted operation tree, and the mapping-space Segal decomposition of step 1 gives the product of its output-tree data. The missing output product is terminal. An internal face composes two adjacent $f_a$ and substitutes at the corresponding adjacent vertices; the initial and final faces remove the first and last levels; a degeneracy inserts unary identities on the wires. Reordering wires is the given permutation action. These descriptions also apply to nullary vertices. For a precise model retaining all higher compatibilities, use [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison]: $\mathfrak C[\Delta^m](a,b)=N(P_{a,b})$, where $P_{a,b}$ is the poset of subsets of $\{a,\ldots,b\}$ containing the endpoints. A subset specifies the cuts at which the interval is evaluated in stages, refinement specifies the comparison, and a chain of refinements specifies its higher comparison simplex. Composition is union of subsets, hence grafting of the subinterval forests. The tree contractions, their chains, grafting and unary-identity data required in the statement are exactly these comparisons after taking the output products. In particular this dictionary includes comparisons involving a discarded branch on a proper face, although that branch contributes nothing to the final composite.

source.place: Construction 2.1.1.7 and Example 2.1.1.21; explicit agent-written leveled-forest and cut-poset expansion. Coherent-realization formula from the cited coherent-nerve node.

proof.text: Now assemble the supplied data. On objects take $X_{\mathbf c}$. For each $f$, step 1 identifies its supplied tuple of output arrows with a point of $M_f(X_{\mathbf c},X_{\mathbf d})$, with the identification retained. Assemble the higher comparisons simultaneously as follows, rather than choosing unrelated inverses of the individual mapping-space equivalences. In the coherent-realization model of step 3, index the comparisons by chains $\sigma$ of operators, intervals $[a,b]$ in $\sigma$, subsets in $P_{a,b}$ and chains of refinements of these subsets; retain all face and degeneracy restrictions of $\sigma$ and all union-composition maps. Compatible maps from these cut nerves into the indicated relative mapping spaces are precisely coherent diagrams over $B$, by the adjunction $\mathfrak C\dashv N_{\mathrm{hc}}$ in [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison]. This can be calculated in a locally Kan simplicial presentation: that node identifies such presentations with quasicategories, including mapping spaces and composition, and its Quillen equivalence identifies their derived diagram spaces over the fixed discrete simplicial category $O^\otimes$. These derived spaces compute the actual section spaces here. Indeed $q$ is an isofibration: a cocartesian lift $u:x\to y$ of a base equivalence induces equivalences $\operatorname{Map}(y,z)\to\operatorname{Map}(x,z)$ for all $z$ by [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion]. On components, at $z=x$ obtain $v$ with $[v][u]=1_x$; at $z=y$ injectivity gives $[u][v]=1_y$. By [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition] this makes $u$ an equivalence. Postcomposition on functor categories is consequently an isofibration by [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-exponentiation]. Its strict fiber over the identity diagram computes the categorical fiber by [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-pullback-limit]. Restrict to the full inert-preserving subcategory; this condition is invariant under equivalences of diagrams because the cocartesian mapping squares are invariant under endpoint equivalences. The same statements hold with prescribed comparison parameters. Taking a derived space of compatible maps, rather than an underived equalizer, retains the specified homotopies. Replace each relative mapping space in this description by the product of its output factors from step 1. The comparison is coherent: restriction of outputs is composition with the inert projections, and the comparison on a union of cuts is precisely substitution of the same operations; the coherent composition compatibility of cocartesian transport is [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport]. Thus this is an objectwise equivalence of the diagrams of spaces of comparisons. Its induced map on their homotopy limits is an equivalence. Here these small limits exist by [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits]; invariance follows by applying the pointwise quasi-inverse, unit and counit from [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] and then their limiting cones. By the dictionary of step 3, the output-side compatible system is exactly the given tree and forest data. Its homotopy fiber on the total-arrow side is therefore contractible and nonempty. Choose a point in that fiber. It supplies the arrows and every composition simplex of a coherent section with the prescribed data. The identity/permutation and inert clauses ensure that its inert edges are $q$-cocartesian. All homotopy limits in this argument are limits of spaces of comparison data; no limit in any fiber $E_c$ is used.

source.place: Definition 2.1.1.10(2), Definition 2.1.3.1; agent-written coherent assembly using the cited cut-poset nerve model and space-limit calculus.

proof.text: Extraction followed by assembly is inverse with its identifications. On each color the comparison is the chosen identification of $X_{(c)}$ with $x_c$; on every operator its output factors are the supplied structure arrows by the defining homotopy fiber of step 4. On an arbitrary tuple the comparison is the inverse of the inert product equivalence, so it is an equivalence, including the empty tuple. There is no independent choice on a transport lift: [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-composition-initiality] makes any such lift initial in $L(X,f)$, and [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] says that the nonempty full category of initial objects is a contractible Kan complex. The higher comparisons of the inverse constructions are those in the homotopy fiber of the limit equivalence of step 4, so they agree on faces, degeneracies and grafting. This is why initiality of separate lifts alone would not have sufficed. Conversely, assembling and then extracting returns the supplied operation data with its specified tree comparisons. A homotopy fiber of an equivalence of spaces is contractible: a quasi-inverse identifies the fiber over $d$ with the space of a point equipped with a path to $d$, which contracts to the constant path. Thus the space of reconstructions together with an identification with the supplied data is contractible.

source.place: Definition 2.1.3.1; contractibility follows from the relative comparison constructed in steps 1-4 and the cited initial-object calculus.

proof.text: To include transformations and higher simplices, perform the construction with a parameter $K$ and base functors constant in the $K$ direction. By [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport], $q_K:\operatorname{Fun}(K,E^\otimes)\to\operatorname{Fun}(K,B)$ is a cocartesian fibration, with cocartesian edges detected at vertices, and its fiber at the constant tuple $\mathbf c$ is $\operatorname{Fun}(K,E_{\mathbf c})$. The definition of the functor simplicial set in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] gives $\operatorname{Fun}(K,\prod_iE_{c_i})=\prod_i\operatorname{Fun}(K,E_{c_i})$ degreewise. Postcomposition by a quasi-inverse of the tuple equivalence gives the corresponding equivalence for $\operatorname{Fun}(K,E_{\mathbf c})$. Step 2's factorization now applies to coherent transformations of $K$-diagrams. In steps 3-4 replace every comparison shape by its product with $K$; faces, degeneracies and union of cuts act on the forest coordinate, while restriction in $K$ acts on the parameter coordinate, so the two commute. The space-limit argument retains all these mixed simplices. In particular $K=\Delta^1$ gives precisely the color maps and operation-naturality simplices of a transformation, and $K=\Delta^n$ gives every higher simplex and its restrictions. The two inverse comparisons in step 5 therefore give coherent natural equivalences of functors on the entire categories of data and sections. They are equivalences by the componentwise criterion in [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. This proves an equivalence of infinity-categories, rather than only an equivalence of their object spaces. No condition on $K$ beyond smallness in the chosen sufficiently large universe is used.

source.place: Remark 2.1.3.4 (parameter categories and pointwise operations), with the explicit exponential and cocartesian-transport argument above.

proof.text: Finally a simplicial map $K'\to K$ restricts each color diagram, each operation arrow and each comparison simplex by precomposition; the forest formulas do exactly the same precomposition. A suboperad restricts the list of colors and operation labels and hence the chains and cut diagrams. Projection to selected colors is evaluation at those one-term tuples. In all three cases the object, operator, face and cut formulas in steps 1-6 agree after restriction; their identification spaces are the same restricted homotopy fibers. This gives the claimed coherent naturality. The only products of objects used are the Segal identifications assumed in the statement, and the remaining limits are spaces of coherence choices, so there is no limit, colimit or presentability hypothesis on the fibers.

source.place: Construction 2.1.1.7, Definition 2.1.3.1 and Remark 2.1.3.4; explicit restriction of the constructed formulas.

proof_origin.place: Proof paragraph 2, middle derived mapping-complex comparison before the inverse limit; supporting coherent operadic foundation. Detailed forest/cut-poset assembly is agent-written from the existing Segal, coherent-nerve and cocartesian-transport statements, with Higher Algebra places checked online in the 2017 edition.
